follow-up time: One year before pregnancy, during pregnancy, and one year postpartum
exposure: previous use of disease modifying therapy (DMT)
Women with relapses in the postpartum period
outcome: Obstetrical complications (e.g., restriction of fetal growth, gestational diabetes)
Newborn complications (e.g., birth asphyxia, low birth weight, malformations)
cohort: 97 women with relapsing-remitting MS diagnosed at least one year before pregnancy, with 127 pregnancies included
finding: While relapse rate decreased during pregnancy, particularly in the third trimester, women experiencing relapses during pregnancy were more likely to have postpartum relapses, impacting disability; DMT use did not appear to influence clinical or obstetrical outcomes.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was performed in 43.3% of patients, mainly due to fetal-pelvic incompatibility, and epidural analgesia was performed in 63.9%, both considered safe procedures.
